answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to anchor its identity to a locked stake: before trading, an agent deposits funds that are slashed if it misbehaves. A single honest agent needs one stake, but a Sybil attacker must fund thousands of separate stakes, like drilling through layer after layer of shale: every fake identity, however polished its sonnet, costs real money upfront and is forfeited on detection, so mass fakery becomes uneconomical.
